exposure: spontaneous vaginal birth with mediolateral episiotomy
spontaneous vaginal delivery with mediolateral episiotomy
cohort: 150 primiparous women between 25 and 35 years old who had a singleton childbirth at least five years previously
finding: Vaginal delivery with mediolateral episiotomy was not associated with urinary and/or fecal incontinence and sexual dysfunction but was associated with decreased sexual functioning as well as sexual desire, arousal and orgasm within postpartum five years.
mod_finding: Women who had a vaginal delivery with mediolateral episiotomy had significantly lower Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) scores, indicating decreased sexual functioning, compared to women who had elective cesarean deliveries or no delivery.
